A common path is: complete postsecondary or university study in electrical automation or electronic information systems; start as a tester or assembly and testing technician; master oscilloscopes, multimeters, and test software; then progress toward research assistant, embedded testing, or automated test development.

Electrical and electronic engineering technologists and technicians work under engineers to build, assemble, test, adjust, and maintain prototypes and systems. They turn designs into operating hardware, troubleshoot faults, and record test data.

paragraphs: In the morning, a technician solders a newly designed board and checks its waveform on a test bench. If data are wrong, they inspect the power supply and then each stage of the signal chain. In the afternoon, they document anomalies and discuss whether the source is the design or a component. Project overtime is common, but every solved problem deepens their understanding of the board.
In one sentence: turn drawings into working prototypes, then test and repair them. Work includes assembly and soldering, testing and adjustment, fault analysis, data records, and documentation.

paragraphs: A score of 6/10 places this occupation in the moderate AI exposure range. AI software increasingly handles drawing, data analysis, and documentation, while people remain central to hardware assembly, testing, and troubleshooting.

Moderate exposure does not mean unemployment. AI takes standardized skills. Automated equipment replaces repetitive wiring, testing, and assembly, but technicians with embedded debugging, automated test development, and system integration skills gain value by working with AI.

Study electrical automation or electronic information systems. Balance theory with laboratory work and electronic design competitions. Add embedded systems and Python-based automated testing so you can write test programs as well as debug boards.

Move from manual testing to automated testing. Learn Python and LabVIEW, and turn repetitive tests into scripts. Progress toward embedded debugging and system integration instead of stopping at soldering and multimeter work.

People with electronics fundamentals can start as testers, but set a schedule. Learn instruments and troubleshooting within a year, then automated testing within two years. On a resume, describe test benches built and fault types resolved rather than listing instruments.

Do not hire technicians on education alone. Test practical skill by asking candidates to solder a board and diagnose a fault. Prioritize people who understand automated testing and embedded systems because they can grow with AI-enabled production.
